issues.detail: The exact p_n_star theorem is derived for the source-defined IHO stochastic channel, not for an unconstrained generic quantum controller. Add one branch-neutral common fixed condition, for example iho_stochastic_channel, stating that evolution uses T=(1-p)S_kappa+p C_gamma, with S_kappa the inverted-harmonic-oscillator squeezing/evolution channel and C_gamma the ancilla measurement-and-reset attenuation channel. Anchor it to lines 130-158, include it in fixed_condition_ids for both claims, and include the same scope in both claim applicability statements. The downstream Player apparatus/background must preserve this exact scope and must not generalize the theorem to arbitrary quantum control. Do not alter the n=1/n=2 private branch conditions, ASTs, parameters, control ranges, readout, or numeric truth.

previous_science_card.assessment: The source provides the exact quantum stochastic-control threshold p_n_star = (exp(n*kappa)-1)/(exp(n*kappa)-exp(-n*gamma)) in Eq. (pstar) at lines 258-260, with the general condition kappa>0, gamma>0 stated at line 74. The routing hint specifies two public controls kappa and gamma on the conservative finite benchmark interval [0.02, 0.42], which lies inside the source-supported positive domain. The private branch parameters n_order_one=1 and n_order_two=2 are supported by the source's statement that p_n_star applies for all n>0 (line 259) and the monotonic sequence p_{n+1}^* > p_n^* (line 262). The readout is the critical intervention probability p_n_star, an exact deterministic theorem. The extraction is faithful to the source; no classical p_c is used as a control. The case is authoring-ready with two claims sharing the same mechanism and readout, differing only in the private n parameter. The previously identified unused parameter pstar_denominator_offset has been removed.

previous_science_card.paper_scope: The paper studies stochastic measurement-and-feedback control of quantum chaotic dynamics, focusing on the quantum Arnold cat map and an inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO) effective model. It derives exact quantum results for the IHO, including a sequence of critical control probabilities p_n^* for operators of order n, given by p_n^* = (e^{n kappa} - 1)/(e^{n kappa} - e^{-n gamma}). The extraction focuses on this exact threshold formula and its dependence on the control strengths kappa and gamma.
